landmarks.name: Merlion
landmarks.facts: Cement, porcelain-plate skin, 70 t. Lim Nang Seng, 1972; moved to the present park in 2002. Spouts water into the bay.
landmarks.bearing_from: faces out across the bay

landmarks.name: Marina Bay Sands
landmarks.facts: Three leaning slab towers, splayed at the base and joined above; the SkyPark deck spans all three and overhangs the north tower by 67 m.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: ArtScience Museum
landmarks.facts: Safdie's lotus: a circular core with ten petal-shaped galleries of different lengths, each skylit at the tip, rising from a lily pond.
landmarks.bearing_from: near circular in plan; a bearing would be meaningless

landmarks.name: Supertree Grove
landmarks.facts: Twelve of the gardens' eighteen Supertrees stand here, 25-50 m tall, planted trunks under steel canopies; the OCBC Skyway links two of them at 22 m.
landmarks.bearing_from: grove laid out roughly along the bay edge

landmarks.name: Singapore Flyer
landmarks.facts: 165 m to the top of a 150 m wheel, so the hub sits at 90 m; 28 capsules outside the rim, carried on an A-frame over a three-storey terminal.
landmarks.bearing_from: wheel plane parallel to the long axis of the terminal footprint

landmarks.name: Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay
landmarks.facts: Two glass shells under more than 7,000 triangular aluminium sunshades - the spikes that earned it 'the durian'.
landmarks.bearing_from: the two shells sit side by side along Esplanade Drive

landmarks.name: The Fullerton
landmarks.facts: The 1928 General Post Office at the mouth of the Singapore River, a Doric colonnade facing the water. It stands directly behind the Merlion in every photograph of it.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: Guoco Tower
landmarks.facts: Singapore's tallest building at 290 m, the cap the Urban Redevelopment Authority allows anywhere near the airport approach. Tanjong Pagar, 2016.
landmarks.bearing_from: square in plan; the value only sets which corner faces the bay

landmarks.name: One Raffles Place
landmarks.facts: Built as OUB Centre in 1986 and one of three towers that stood at exactly 280 m for twenty years, the height limit of the day.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: Republic Plaza
landmarks.facts: Kisho Kurokawa, 1995: a square plan that turns into an octagon as it rises, and the third of the 280 m trio on Raffles Place.
landmarks.bearing_from: square in plan, rotated to an octagon above

landmarks.name: UOB Plaza One
landmarks.facts: Kenzo Tange, 1992, at the mouth of the Singapore River: a square tower that steps back three times to a flat top.
landmarks.bearing_from: square in plan

landmarks.name: The Pinnacle@Duxton
landmarks.facts: Fifty storeys of public housing in seven towers, linked at the 26th and 50th floors by skybridges that run the length of the block. The tallest public residential building anywhere.
landmarks.bearing_from: the rows run roughly north-north-east, from the footprints beneath them

landmarks.name: Masjid Sultan
landmarks.facts: The 1824 mosque rebuilt in 1932 at the heart of Kampong Glam: one great golden onion dome over the prayer hall, four smaller ones at the corners, and a base ring of glass bottles donated by worshippers who could afford nothing else.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of that footprint

landmarks.name: National Gallery Singapore
landmarks.facts: City Hall and the old Supreme Court, joined under one filigree canopy in 2015. The dome is where every colonial-era photograph of Singapore points.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of the old Supreme Court footprint beside the anchor

landmarks.name: Henderson Waves
landmarks.facts: Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge, 274 m long and 36 m above Henderson Road, carried on seven curved ribs that alternate above and below the deck.
landmarks.bearing_from: the bridge crosses Henderson Road roughly east-south-east; no footprint, because it is a bridge

landmarks.name: Chinese Garden Pagoda
landmarks.facts: The seven-storey pagoda of the 1975 Chinese Garden at Jurong Lake, modelled on the Linggu Temple pagoda in Nanjing. The one landmark in the western half of the island that can be seen from a distance.
landmarks.bearing_from: octagonal in plan; a bearing would be meaningless

landmarks.name: Jewel Changi Airport
landmarks.facts: Safdie's glass toroid between the terminals, with the 40 m Rain Vortex falling through its oculus - the tallest indoor waterfall there is. The only landmark in the east of the study area.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of that footprint

landmarks.name: Bangunan Sultan Ibrahim
landmarks.facts: Palmer and Turner, 1936-40, on Bukit Timbalan: a Saracenic tower over a colonial block with Malay roofs. The tallest building in Malaya before independence, and still the one JB's skyline is read from.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of the Bukit Timbalan footprint

landmarks.name: Masjid Sultan Abu Bakar
landmarks.facts: Victorian-Moorish state mosque of 1900 on a terrace above the strait; four corner minarets built as clock towers rather than domes.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of the footprint above the strait

landmarks.name: Komtar JBCC
landmarks.facts: The mall and tower above JB's city centre, opened 2014, the bulk at the top of Jalan Wong Ah Fook.
landmarks.bearing_from: near square in plan

landmarks.name: The Astaka
landmarks.facts: Twin residential towers at Bukit Senyum, 278.8 m and 255.6 m - the tallest things in Johor Bahru and the first thing visible from the Singapore side.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis through the twin towers

landmarks.name: Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar
landmarks.facts: The Johor state assembly at Kota Iskandar, the administrative centre built at Iskandar Puteri in 2009 in a Moorish-Andalusian idiom. Twenty kilometres west of the old capital, and the reason the study area reaches that far.
landmarks.bearing_from: long axis of that footprint

landmarks.name: Johor Bahru City Square
landmarks.facts: The mall that faces the CIQ across Jalan Wong Ah Fook, with a 36-storey office tower over it. For most people crossing the Causeway on foot it is the first building in Malaysia they walk into.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: Bangunan Sultan Iskandar (CIQ)
landmarks.facts: Malaysia's customs, immigration and quarantine complex at the north end of the Causeway: the building this whole study's cross-border travel times pass through.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: Woodlands Checkpoint
landmarks.facts: Singapore's end of the Causeway. Paired with the CIQ building, the two mark the only land crossing in the study area.
landmarks.bearing_from: footprint long axis

landmarks.name: Johor-Singapore Causeway
landmarks.facts: The 1,056 m embankment of 1923 carrying road, railway and a water pipeline between Woodlands and Johor Bahru - the only land crossing in the study area, and the thing every cross-border walk in this dashboard has to pass through.
landmarks.bearing_from: the KTM track's heading across the strait, 1.4496,103.7703 to 1.4588,103.7673 in the basemap's rail layer
